questions.stem: A FastAPI handler is async def and calls the synchronous Gemini SDK, which blocks for 2 s. Cloud Run concurrency is 80, CPU is 8%, instances stay at 2. What is happening?
options: Cold starts
The blocking call freezes the event loop, so one instance serves one request at a time while up to 80 queue; the autoscaler sees neither high concurrency nor high CPU and does not add instances
Gemini quota
Memory pressure
questions.explanation: Use def (threadpool) or an async client, and size containerConcurrency to what one instance can really serve. Low CPU with deep queues is the signature of a blocked loop.

questions.stem: Which TWO Cloud Run settings matter most for long streamed tutor answers?
options: Request timeout long enough for the longest answer (default 300 s, up to 60 minutes)
Max instances 1
CPU allocation: request-based billing throttles CPU outside requests, so work after the response is sent needs always-allocated CPU
Session affinity is required for SSE
Ingress all
questions.explanation: Timeouts cap streams; CPU allocation decides whether background work after a response runs. Streaming itself works with request-based CPU while the request is open.

questions.stem: The catalog API (service account A) calls the tutor agent on Cloud Run with no public access. What is the standard setup?
options: Give allUsers the invoker role and check a header
Grant A roles/run.invoker on the tutor service; A fetches a Google-signed ID token with the tutor's URL as audience and sends it as a Bearer token; the service may verify the token and caller again
Share a static API key in Secret Manager
Use the same service account for both
questions.explanation: IAM at the edge plus ID tokens is the documented service-to-service pattern; in-app verification of audience and caller is defence in depth.

questions.stem: In ADK, where do you put a guardrail that refuses off-topic questions without spending a model call?
options: In the instruction text only
A before_model_callback that returns a response and skips the model call
An after_tool_callback
The session service
questions.explanation: before_model_callback can inspect the request and return an LlmResponse to short-circuit the model. after_model_callback can rewrite responses (the answer-leak check).

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about ADK sessions and state are correct?
options: Session state holds data that persists across the turns of one conversation (for example the current lesson)
InMemorySessionService is a production choice on Cloud Run with several instances
A persistent session service (database or Agent Runtime's managed sessions) is needed when instances scale out or restart
Sessions are only available in Java
State is sent to the model automatically in full on every turn
questions.explanation: In-memory sessions vanish on restart and are not shared across instances. Choose a database-backed service on Cloud Run, or Agent Runtime's managed sessions and memory.

questions.stem: Cloud Run or Agent Runtime (formerly Agent Engine) for the tutor agent?
options: Agent Runtime is always cheaper

Cloud Run gives a container you control (FastAPI, middleware, any library) and fits a team that already runs containers; Agent Runtime gives managed sessions, memory and agent ops with less control. Decide on control vs managed features
Cloud Run cannot run ADK
Agent Runtime cannot use tools
questions.explanation: Both run ADK; the trade-off is control and familiarity vs managed agent services. This posting names Cloud Run.

questions.stem: The tutor uses McpToolset to connect to a shared MCP server that also exposes write tools for other agents. Which control actually prevents the tutor from writing?
options: A sentence in the instruction saying never to call the write tools
tool_filter on the McpToolset listing only the read tools, plus an allow-list in the agent and per-caller authorization on the server
A higher temperature
Using streamable HTTP instead of stdio
questions.explanation: Instructions are requests that injected content can override. Not offering the tool, refusing it in code and authorizing per caller are controls.

questions.stem: The model asks get_learner_progress(learner_id="lrn-bo") during lrn-ada's session. What is the right design?
options: Trust it; the model knows best
Bind learner and course to the session in the tool implementation (from tool_context.state or the server's session), so the model never chooses whose data to read
Ask the learner to confirm
Return both learners
questions.explanation: Letting the model pick identifiers makes the agent a confused deputy. Tools take only what the model should choose (a query, a lesson id) and read identity from the session.

questions.stem: Which ADK workflow agent fits 'retrieve, then draft a hint, then check the hint does not reveal the answer, always in that order'?
options: LoopAgent with no exit
SequentialAgent with three sub-agents (or one LLM agent plus deterministic steps)
ParallelAgent
A single agent with no tools
questions.explanation: Fixed order is a workflow, not an autonomous agent. Keep deterministic steps deterministic; use a loop only for evaluator-optimizer patterns with a bounded number of rounds.

questions.stem: Your MCP server returns whole lesson bodies (20,000 characters) and raw API objects. Which TWO changes follow tool-design guidance?
options: Return compact, task-shaped results with renamed fields, and truncate long text with a flag
Add more tools that mirror every REST endpoint
Write descriptions that say when to use the tool and what it returns
Return stack traces so the model can debug
Accept learner_id so the model can choose
questions.explanation: Tools for agents are an API for a model: fewer, task-shaped tools, small outputs and descriptions the model can choose by improve accuracy and cost.

questions.stem: Which TWO are reasons to choose pgvector on Cloud SQL or AlloyDB over RAG Engine for the course tutor?
options: Vectors live next to relational data, so course and tenant filters are ordinary SQL in the same query
No tuning or operations are needed
You need full control of chunking, indexes (HNSW, IVFFlat) and query plans
It includes managed ingestion of PDFs
It is the only option that supports metadata
questions.explanation: pgvector gives control and co-location at the price of owning tuning and operations. RAG Engine manages ingestion, chunking, embedding and retrieval; Agent Search adds managed ranking and grounding with the least code.

questions.stem: A learner must only retrieve chunks from their own course. Where does that filter go?
options: Retrieve the global top-k, then drop other courses
In the retrieval query itself (WHERE course_id = $1 in pgvector, a metadata filter in RAG Engine or Agent Search), because it is access control
In the prompt: 'only use your course'
In the Angular app
questions.explanation: Post-filtering returns fewer than k results and is one forgotten line away from a leak. Filter first; it is an authorization rule.

questions.stem: Recall@5 is 1.0 for both chunking strategies on your 32-question set, but MRR differs (0.92 vs 0.94). What do you report?
options: Recall@5 proves they are equal
recall@5 saturates on a small corpus; report recall@1 and MRR, note that one question moves a metric by about 3 points, and label more questions before declaring a winner
Pick the one with fewer chunks
Drop MRR
questions.explanation: Small labeled sets have wide uncertainty. Use metrics that still discriminate and grow the set.

questions.stem: Why does heading-aware chunking usually beat fixed-size windows for a tutor that must cite sections?
options: It produces more chunks
Chunks align with the citation unit (a section), carry the heading's vocabulary, and never mix two sections' text, so the cited section is right more often
It needs no embeddings
Fixed windows are not allowed by RAG Engine
questions.explanation: Keep lesson and section ids as metadata on every chunk; structure-aware chunking makes citations precise.

questions.stem: You switch embedding models. What else must happen?
options: Nothing
Re-embed the whole corpus with the new model (vectors from different models are not comparable), run the retrieval eval before cutting over, and use the right task type for documents vs queries
Only re-embed new documents
Lower the top-k
questions.explanation: Mixed-model vectors silently degrade retrieval. Re-embedding costs money and time; build the new index beside the old one and swap.

questions.stem: After a content merge, citations point one lesson off and recall@3 drops from 0.90 to 0.05. The embedding model also changed the day before. Which evidence separates the causes?
options: None; roll back both
The eval history: recall stayed 0.90 after the model change and fell only after the content merge; then compare stored lesson ids with each file's front matter
Ask Gemini
Check the Cloud Run logs for 500s
questions.explanation: Change one variable at a time and read the timeline. Ids derived from file order instead of content shift when a file is added.

questions.stem: What is reranking in a retrieval pipeline?
options: Sorting results alphabetically
A second stage that rescores the top N candidates from fast vector or hybrid search with a more expensive relevance model before taking the top k
Re-embedding the corpus
Changing chunk size
questions.explanation: Retrieve broadly and cheaply, then rerank precisely. RAG Engine and Agent Search both offer ranking options; measure the gain with the same labeled set.

questions.stem: Which layering of tutor evals is the most cost-effective in CI?
options: LLM-as-judge on everything first

Deterministic checks first (schema valid, answer key, citation exists), then retrieval metrics on labeled questions, then judge metrics with a custom rubric (does not reveal the answer, grounded) on a sample
Only human review
Only production metrics
questions.explanation: Cheap, exact checks catch most regressions; judge metrics are for what code cannot check. The Gen AI evaluation service supports custom rubrics and agent trajectory metrics.

questions.stem: Which TWO does agent evaluation add beyond scoring the final answer?
options: Trajectory: whether the agent called the expected tools with the expected arguments in a sensible order
The color of the UI
Checking that forbidden tools (writes) were never called
The model's training data
The number of Cloud Run instances
questions.explanation: Agent evals look at the path as well as the answer: expected tool calls, and no forbidden ones. ADK eval sets and the Gen AI evaluation service both support this.

questions.stem: How should the retrieval eval run so it actually protects production?
options: As an advisory report someone may read
As a blocking CI step on changes to chunking, embedding model, index settings and content, comparing to a stored baseline with a tolerance; the baseline moves only in a reviewed change
Weekly by hand
Only after incidents
questions.explanation: An advisory gate is how w5-t1 happened. Make it block, and treat the baseline like code.

questions.stem: When is supervised tuning of Gemini the wrong tool?
options: When you need a consistent output format and house style
When the model needs fresh or changing knowledge (new course content): use retrieval instead
When a cheaper model must match a larger one on a narrow task
When prompts have grown very long
questions.explanation: Tuning teaches format, style and narrow behaviour; it does not keep up with new facts. Try prompting, few-shot and RAG first; tune when the eval says the cheaper path is not enough.

questions.stem: Which TWO belong in preparing a supervised tuning dataset?
options: Deduplicate examples and remove anything that overlaps the held-out evaluation set
Include the evaluation set in training to boost scores
Use the documented JSONL conversation format (system instruction, user and model turns) with a validation split
Prefer thousands of noisy examples over a few hundred clean ones
Shuffle the held-out set into validation
questions.explanation: Leakage inflates scores; clean data beats volume. Follow the format in the prepare-data guide.

questions.stem: Tuned Flash-Lite: valid 1.00, correct 0.90, 0.13 USD per 1,000 items. Few-shot Flash: valid 0.96, correct 0.90, 1.49 USD. Held-out set: 50 items. What is the strongest conclusion?
options: Tuned is more accurate
They are statistically tied on correctness at n=50; cost (about 11x) and latency favour tuned, provided its training data did not leak the held-out set
Few-shot is better because it is a bigger model
Neither can ship
questions.explanation: With 50 items a proportion near 0.9 has roughly +-8 points of uncertainty. Decide on what the numbers can distinguish, and check for leakage before trusting the tuned result.

questions.stem: The docs recommend a setting for thinking on tuned tasks. Which?
options: Maximum thinking budget
Thinking budget 0 or thinking level minimal on the tuned model
Thinking only in the system instruction
Disable structured output
questions.explanation: Per the supervised tuning docs, set thinking to off or minimal for tuned models; tuned narrow tasks gain little from it and pay latency.

questions.stem: The index (created_at, learner_id) exists, yet WHERE learner_id = ? AND course_id = ? AND date(created_at) >= ? ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20 reads 41M rows. Which TWO explain it?
options: The index leads with the range column, so it cannot narrow by learner first
Wrapping created_at in date() prevents using the index for the range
The table needs VACUUM FULL
LIMIT disables indexes
PostgreSQL cannot use composite indexes
questions.explanation: Equality columns first, range last: (learner_id, course_id, created_at) serves the filter and the order. Predicates must not wrap the indexed column (or use an expression index).

questions.stem: Which EXPLAIN ANALYZE detail most directly shows a missing or unusable index?
options: Planning Time
A large 'Rows Removed by Filter' compared with rows returned, on a scan of the whole table or index
Buffers: shared hit
The presence of Limit
questions.explanation: Reading millions of rows to return eleven means the predicate is applied after reading, not used to find rows.

questions.stem: quiz_attempt grows 6M rows a month and academic records must be kept 4 years. Which TWO fit?
options: Range-partition by month on created_at and drop or detach partitions past retention after archiving
DELETE old rows nightly
Keep indexes that lead with tenant and learner on each partition for dashboard queries
One index per column
Store attempts in the agent's memory
questions.explanation: Partition pruning and partition drops beat large deletes; local indexes keep queries fast. Analytics belong in BigQuery.

questions.stem: You must add a NOT NULL column to a 41M-row table with the app running. What is the expand-and-contract sequence?
options: ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL in one migration
Add the column nullable, deploy code that writes it, backfill in batches, then add the constraint (NOT VALID then VALIDATE for checks), then make reads depend on it
Rename the table
Do it during a maintenance window only
questions.explanation: Expand, migrate, contract: each step is backward compatible with the running version, so deploys and rollbacks stay safe.

questions.stem: Cloud Run scales the catalog API to 30 instances with a Hikari pool of 10 each against a Cloud SQL instance with max_connections 100. What is the risk and a fix?
options: None

300 possible connections exceed the database limit; cap instances, size the pool to the instance count, or put a pooler (for example the Cloud SQL connector with managed pooling or PgBouncer) in front
Increase the pool to 50
Use H2 in production
questions.explanation: Connection math belongs in capacity planning: instances x pool size must fit the database.

questions.stem: A tuned model is pinned to its base model version. What operational duty follows?
options: None; tuned models never change
Track the base version's retirement date and plan to re-tune on a newer base and re-run the same eval before the old one retires
Retrain every day
Switch to few-shot when it retires
questions.explanation: Tuned endpoints inherit the base model's lifecycle. Keep the dataset and eval ready to re-tune.
